owner: No configuration owner today: constants. A Runtime-host operator could own a lowering knob, but none exists; AD-08 says F3 limits stay floors, at most host-owned lowering.

monotone_narrowing.relation: Lower depth/node/byte limit only rejects more inputs (min(code,registry)); absent keeps code constant. Relation is trivially monotone but not the deciding criterion.

consumer.evidence: Constants 32/10000/1048576 are literals in the function body (safe_executor.py:155,161,170,177); max_bytes is a keyword default only. No caller passes a different value (grep: callers at safe_executor.py:200,289 and openshell_environment.py:57 pass none). No Registry reader exists for it; the Runtime Registry adapters reach LocalExecutionPolicy only. validate_snapshot re-admits at effect time (safe_executor.py:889) and the sandbox worker re-runs it from image-baked code (openshell_worker.py:8,18), so a host-side lowered value would diverge from the worker.

immutable_floor: Ceilings 32 / 10000 / 1 MiB, 256-bit int and finite-float rules, exact-builtin-type requirement, order (admit before deepcopy/json.dumps). These define the canonical admission domain shared with the worker image.
case_for_eligible: Narrow-only DoS bound; operators with small payloads gain a tighter limit; plan 4 lists 'approved resource limits' as migratable.
case_against: Plan M6 excludes mandatory admission floors (depth/node/text/process limits); AD-08 keeps F3 limits floors; no consumer or config surface; effect-time and in-image re-admission means a lowered host value creates split admission (host refuses what worker accepts, or an in-flight frozen envelope fails validate_snapshot at execute time -> policy_denial); operational value is low.
blocking_decision: Residual preference only (not blocking): does the Architect want a host-owned LOWERING knob for Runtime admission budgets (3 scalars) with propagation into the sandbox worker image? If yes it is a separate NEW feature, not a migration of the current constants.
